main_text.p: Motricis sunt, per quæ facultas animalis motus animales in corpore ciet.
Suntq; motricis vel ζωϊκῆς[?], vel αἰσθη-τικῆς[?] organa.
Motricis ζωϊκῆς seu vitalis sunt vel Respiratricis vel Micatricis facultatis membra.
Organa respirati-onis,Respirationis organa sunt, quæ famulantur aëris in corpus inspirationi & expirationi.
Suntq; duorum generum. Primi generis sunt Diaphragma, & Pulmo.

Diaphra-gma.DIAPHRAGMA, est quasi continuus musculꝰ in medio nerveus, in circuitu carneus, utrinq; membranis vestitus, inter thoracem & ventrem inferiorem situs, quo contracto thorax dilatatur, & fit inspiratio, laxato vero thorax in se concidit, & fit expiratio.

Pulmo,Pulmo est membrum respirationis spongiosum, rarum, molle, spumæ sanguinis concretæ simile, in spacio supremo thoracis ad dexteram nonnihil inclinans, quo dilatato, aër attrahitur, attracto vero, idem redditur.

page.notes: The Greek words "ζωϊκῆς", "αἰσθητικῆς" and "τικῆς" are only partly legible in the scan (the Greek is set with a hyphen at the line end), so they are marked [?]. The note "Organa respirati-onis," is set in italic and runs over three lines in the margin. The paragraph beginning "Pulmo autè membrana" continues on the next page; its last word is cut off at the foot as catchword "direm-". The "ꝰ" in "musculꝰ" stands for printed superscript 9 (us), as in the original.
